title: Chip-card deployment can reduce future EBT theft exposure without restoring theft losses
source_unit: New Jersey Human Services EBT chip-card fraud-prevention rollout
geography: New Jersey SNAP and Work First New Jersey cardholders

observations.period: July 2026 EBT chip-card pilot and planned statewide rollout

denominator.unit: counties in the initial SNAP/WFNJ chip-card pilot; statewide rollout planned

prevention_control.value: EMV chip-enabled EBT cards introduced in a three-county pilot; replacement-card requests statewide receive a chip card

recourse_boundary.value: Electronically stolen SNAP and WFNJ benefits on or after December 21, 2024 are not eligible for replacement under the stated federal funding rule

benefit_continuity.value: The chip-card route is designed to prevent future theft; the public release does not report restored stolen benefits, food-gap duration, or later household security

observations.method: Structured extraction from the official New Jersey Human Services press release and EBT theft guidance; prevention, replacement-card access, and post-December-2024 replacement ineligibility are retained as separate stages.
observations.uncertainty: The public sources do not disclose pilot uptake, card activation, prevented theft, victim-level replacement, food adequacy, substitution, appeal outcomes, trust, or exit.
observations.subgroup: New Jersey SNAP and WFNJ cardholders; initial chip-card pilot counties are Cumberland, Essex, and Mercer.
observations.counterinterpretation: A more secure card can lower future exposure while leaving prior electronically stolen benefits unrecovered; prevention and remedy receipt are distinct outcomes.

observations.period: September 2026 statewide chip-card availability and pilot transaction report

denominator.unit: New Jersey SNAP and WFNJ participants; statewide count not disclosed in the release

statewide_distribution.value: EBT chip cards reported distributed statewide

chip_transactions.unit: more than chip transactions during the pilot

activation_and_transfer_rule.value: Benefits automatically transfer when the new card is activated; remaining-county old cards stop working October 20, 2026 and new cards not activated by November 20, 2026 require a replacement request
activation_and_transfer_rule.unit: reported operational timing and account-transfer rule

observations.method: Structured extraction from the official New Jersey statewide-availability release; rollout and transaction counts are retained as implementation outputs, not as unique-user activation or prevented-theft rates.
observations.uncertainty: The release and implementation page do not disclose unique cardholders, activation rate, transaction denominator, prevented theft, replacement of prior losses, food adequacy, or later household outcomes; the deadline and transfer rules do not prove individual usability.
observations.subgroup: New Jersey SNAP and WFNJ participants; transaction counts refer to the pilot phase and are not unique people.
observations.counterinterpretation: Statewide distribution and early secure-payment use demonstrate implementation reach, but transaction volume can coexist with unmeasured nonactivation, inaccessible replacement, prior unrecovered loss, or continued fraud.

related_sources.claim: New Jersey's current theft guidance states that electronically stolen SNAP and WFNJ benefits on or after December 21, 2024 are not eligible for replacement and directs cardholders toward prevention controls.

The chip-card implementation page describes statewide mailing, automatic benefit transfer upon activation, old-card deactivation and activation deadlines, and replacement instructions; it does not establish individual activation, prevented theft, or household recovery.

boundary: This record establishes a named state prevention and card-access response plus a federal-policy boundary on replacement of later electronic theft. It does not establish prevented theft, restoration of stolen benefits, food security, adequacy, trust, or exit.
